html:
The Karkin were an Ohlone people of the Carquinez Strait, where San Francisco Bay meets the Sacramento River delta, in Northern California. The strait is named after them.

Their language, the most distinct of the Ohlone languages, is known only from a short word list that a Spanish missionary took down in 1821. Like their neighbours the Bay Miwok and the Chochenyo, they were drawn into the Spanish missions from the late 1700s and ceased to exist as a separate group.
